body_es: Amazon VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) es la capa de red fundamental en AWS que permite crear redes virtuales aisladas dentro de la nube. Una VPC abarca todas las AZs de una región y se divide en subredes (subnets) que residen en una sola AZ. Las subredes públicas tienen acceso a Internet mediante un Internet Gateway (IGW) adjunto a la VPC y una ruta hacia él en la tabla de rutas. Las subredes privadas no tienen acceso directo a Internet; los recursos privados que necesitan salida usan un NAT Gateway (servicio gestionado) o una NAT Instance en una subred pública. Las Network ACLs (NACLs) actúan a nivel de subred, son stateless (las reglas de entrada y salida son independientes), y procesan reglas en orden numérico. Los Security Groups actúan a nivel de instancia/interfaz, son stateful (el retorno de tráfico permitido es automático), y solo admiten reglas de permiso (todo lo no explícito es denegado). Para el SAA-C03, los conceptos clave son: VPC Peering para conectar dos VPCs (no transitivo), Transit Gateway para conexiones hub-and-spoke entre múltiples VPCs y redes on-premises, VPC Endpoints (Gateway para S3/DynamoDB, Interface para otros servicios) para acceder a servicios de AWS sin salir a Internet, y Flow Logs para auditoría de tráfico a nivel de VPC, subred o interfaz de red.
body_en: Amazon VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) provides an isolated virtual network environment within AWS, spanning all Availability Zones in a region. Subnets are subdivisions of a VPC tied to a single AZ. Public subnets have a route to an Internet Gateway (IGW) attached to the VPC, allowing instances with public IPs to send and receive Internet traffic. Private subnets route outbound traffic through a NAT Gateway (managed, highly available per AZ) or a NAT Instance (self-managed EC2) placed in a public subnet. Network ACLs (NACLs) are stateless, subnet-level firewalls that evaluate both inbound and outbound rules independently in numbered order; a return packet needs an explicit allow rule. Security Groups are stateful, instance-level firewalls — return traffic is automatically allowed, and only permit rules exist (implicit deny for everything else). For the SAA-C03 exam: VPC Peering connects two VPCs directly (non-transitive — each pair needs its own peering connection), while Transit Gateway provides a centralized hub for connecting multiple VPCs and on-premises networks transitively. VPC Endpoints (Gateway type for S3 and DynamoDB, Interface type for 100+ other services) route traffic to AWS services over the private AWS backbone, never touching the public Internet. VPC Flow Logs capture network metadata at VPC, subnet, or ENI level for security analysis.
example_code:
# Create VPC
aws ec2 create-vpc --cidr-block 10.0.0.0/16

# Create public subnet
aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id vpc-123 --cidr-block 10.0.1.0/24 --availability-zone us-east-1a

# Create Internet Gateway
aws ec2 create-internet-gateway

# Attach to VPC
aws ec2 attach-internet-gateway --internet-gateway-id igw-123 --vpc-id vpc-123

# Create route table
aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id vpc-123
